readings.title: 守护脆弱的地球
readings.text: Our planet's biodiversity is one of its greatest treasures. Forests, rivers, wetlands, and remote islands are home to countless forms of wildlife. Yet human activity puts this balance at risk. When large farms spread pesticide and herbicide on their fields, rain can carry the chemicals into streams and lakes. There the substances may oxidize and slowly turn the water acidic, harming fish and frogs. Fine aerosol particles from factories and vehicles drift through the sky and fall back to the earth, where they enter the food chain. In the marine world, seals and seabirds sometimes swallow plastic, while older industrial sites still leak mercury into the mud. Some nations build a nuclear reactor to make electricity with low carbon emissions, but communities near mountains and coasts fear accidents and long-term waste. Researchers and local groups study these threats and propose practical steps: plant native trees, cut chemical use, and protect wild areas. Scientists gather statistics showing that tremendous damage can follow a single spill, and they urge farmers to spray more carefully. Schools take children to nearby hills and shores so they can observe nature with their own eyes. Different regions of the world share the same oceans, so one country's pollution becomes everyone's problem. When people understand how daily choices shape the environment, they begin to act. Saving water, sorting waste, and choosing clean transport may seem small, but together they protect the systems that keep our world alive for the next generation. 🔁 Review: door, window, table, man, woman, boy, girl, baby, teacher, letter, paper, store, stop, hot, cold, air, price.

readings.text: Modern medicine helps people live longer and healthier lives. A surgeon can repair a damaged heart, while a biologist studies the tiny cells that keep our bodies working. Good healthcare depends not only on hospitals but also on prevention: regular exercise, balanced food, and personal fitness. Researchers and scientists spend years testing new treatments, and their work is studied by teams around the world. New techniques let experts repair organs that once could not be saved, and careful study of consequences helps them avoid harm. Students who train to become nurses must memorize hundreds of terms and practise on models before they meet real patients. When accidents cause injuries, quick action and clear solutions save lives. Local hospitals now share data through computer systems, so a doctor can see a patient's history within seconds. Public campaigns teach children to wash hands and eat well, which reduces infection rates in crowded cities. Although money and equipment matter, the kindness of nurses often helps recovery as much as medicine does. As technology improves, even small clinics in remote villages can connect with experts far away. The goal of health science is simple: give every person a fair chance to grow, work, and care for the people they love. 🔁 Review: office, cost, hotel, visit, movie, picture, size, color, want, happy, bad, free, sure, know, thanks, close, get.

readings.title: 科技如何改变生活
readings.text: Technology surrounds us in ways our grandparents could never imagine. A small calculator can solve in seconds what once took a whole afternoon. Radar and satellite systems help airplanes avoid storms and guide ships across the ocean. Inside every phone and laptop, a tiny circuit moves electricity through paths thinner than a hair, while electrical signals carry our messages around the planet. Engineers design these devices, and many of them learned programming as teenagers. Today computers and networks connect schools, banks, and homes, so a student can attend a class on the other side of the world. Some machines are automatic: they sort mail, park cars, and even clean floors without help. A friendly android robot may soon help older people with daily tasks, and useful apps remind us to drink water or learn a new word. Experts say an instant message can reach anyone with a signal, yet this speed also creates worries about privacy. None of this appeared overnight; each tool grew from decades of patient experiment. Still, technology also brings challenges, such as screen time and lost concentration. The task for the next generation is to use these powers wisely, keeping human judgement at the centre while letting machines handle the routine work that once filled our days. When we understand both the gifts and the risks, we can build a future where technology serves people instead of replacing them. A phone's battery and a laptop's screen are the quiet tools behind modern life. 🔁 Review: wait, call, wear, high, fast, beautiful, easy, full, again, fire, order, trip, drug, career, consider, develop, interview.

readings.titleEn: The Way of Learning at School
readings.text: Going to university is more than attending lectures; it is learning how to think. Each semester, a student receives a syllabus that lists the topics and the dates of every test. Life on campus means balancing homework, friends, and sleep. A good lecturer explains difficult ideas clearly, yet real understanding comes when a mentor or tutor sits with you and answers your questions. At first, every first-year student feels like a novice, but with practice the work becomes easier. Weekly lessons build on one another, so missing one class can leave a gap. To prepare for a quiz, a clever learner reviews notes each evening and keeps them organized. Many students studying late at the library discover that teaching a friend is the best way to remember. Groups that meet in the cafe often solve problems faster than anyone alone. When the deadline for a big project arrives, the whole class works together late into the night. After graduation, some choose postgraduate study, while others join companies that value clear thinking. Universities are not only places of exams; they are communities where young people learn to argue with evidence and to listen with respect. Mistakes are not failures; they show where more effort is needed. By the final exam, a student who started nervous can explain the material with confidence. Education is not only about grades; it trains the mind to ask better questions and to keep learning long after the last bell rings. 🔁 Review: apply, population, facilities, income, growth, force, supplies, continue, benefits, believe, organization, effect, role, supply, necessary, according, capital.

Good techniques turn a cheap cut of meat into a soft meal, and a spoon of cocoa powder can make a plain drink feel like a treat. Some dishes need hours of slow heat, while others are ready in minutes as an instant snack. A home kitchen also shows basic chemistry: sugar turns golden, and dough rises as small bubbles form. Beyond taste, sharing a meal builds friendship and calm. In many cultures, the evening meal is the one time the whole family sits without phones. Learning to cook is a skill that lasts a lifetime, saving money and improving health. Even a beginner can start with three ingredients and grow from there, discovering that a little care turns plain food into something worth remembering. When children learn to cook, they also learn maths through measuring and reading through following steps, so the kitchen becomes a quiet classroom. 🔁 Review: investment, decision, summer, allow, purpose, operation, opportunity, ability, likely, responsibility, foreign, feature, police, documents, communication, approach, developed.

readings.title: 社会与法治
readings.titleEn: Society and the Rule of Law
readings.text: A healthy society depends on trust and fair rules. Politicians propose ideas, but representatives must listen to the people who elected them. When someone breaks the law, the courts review the evidence and decide a fair response. Prisoners who show real change may later return to society and rebuild their lives. New immigrants often bring skills and fresh energy, though they also face the hard task of learning a new language and culture. Clear regulations protect workers from unsafe conditions and keep food safe to eat. A society's heritage of fair principles is as important as its roads and bridges, because it teaches each generation what justice means. Still, no system is perfect; corruption and inequality remain real problems. Citizens who read the news and ask questions help keep power honest. Community groups that clean parks or help the elderly show that small actions matter. Education and open debate are the best tools against fear and misunderstanding. In the end, a strong society is one where every person feels they belong and has a voice that counts, and where the law serves people rather than the other way around. When neighbours help one another after a storm, they show that fairness is built in daily life, not only in courtrooms. A town that listens to its quietest voices is stronger than one that silences them. 🔁 Review: reserve, schedule, budget, debt, menu, relative, copy, cash, employment, overall, commission, package, engine, album, administration, exchange, electronic.

Visitors who learn a few words of the local language are welcomed with smiles, and quiet restaurants often serve the best meals. Local shops sell crafts made by hand, supporting families that have worked there for generations. Remote islands and quiet mountains remind us how vast and varied the earth is, and how small our daily worries can seem. Different regions keep different traditions, from music to food to festival. In a coastal town you may stroll down a flower-lined avenue and hear a language you do not speak, yet still feel at home. When we return home, we carry not just photos but a wider sense of what it means to be human among many kinds of people. Travel teaches that the world is large and kind, and that most strangers are simply people whose story we have not yet heard. readings.title: 情绪与内心
readings.text: Our emotions guide many choices we never pause to explain. Old memories can surface without warning and change our mood for hours. Two sisters may react to the same event in opposite ways, because their minds hold different stories. When we feel afraid, our hearts beat faster and the body prepares to act. A clever person notices these signals instead of ignoring them. Some find calm through spiritual practice, while others talk with a friend who listens without judgement. Life is not always neat; messy feelings are normal and useful. A nasty comment can hurt more than a physical blow, so kind words matter. We sometimes catch ourselves wondering whether we are enough, and that quiet doubt is part of being human. Our behaviour toward others often reflects the mood we carry inside, so learning to name what we feel is the first step to kindness. Naming what we feel, anger, joy, shame, or hope, gives us power over it. Shared laughter can cheer a room, and a single act of care can steady a shaking heart. In the end, understanding our inner life helps us treat others with the same patience we wish for ourselves on hard days, and turns quiet fear into steady courage. Writing in a diary helps us notice these shifts, and a walk outside or a favourite song can shift a dark afternoon toward light. Tiny kindnesses, more than grand plans, steady the heart. 🔁 Review: owner, retail, senior, trial, entire, educational, alternative, session, assistance, northern, otherwise, recommended, background, maintenance, brands, winter, monitor.

readings.title: 想象中的怪兽与英雄
readings.titleEn: Monsters and Heroes of the Imagination
readings.text: Long before science explained the stars, people told stories of fantasy to make sense of fear. A dragon guarding a mountain, a ghost wandering an old house, or a monster beneath the lake all gave shape to the unknown. Horror tales made listeners hold their breath, while epic poems sang of brave men and women who faced danger without flinching. In these stories, heroes do not win because they are strongest, but because they refuse to quit. A rusty sword in a museum may once have been carried into battle, and the glory of that age lives on in song. The kings and the gods of the oldest tales appeared as symbols of hope and warning, teaching listeners right from wrong without a single lecture. Such tales teach courage and kindness more clearly than any rule book. Children learn that being afraid is normal, and that help can appear from the most unlikely friend. Modern films still borrow these ancient shapes, proving that the hunger for story is part of us. Whether the setting is a village, a spaceship, or a hidden forest, we recognise the same hopes: to protect the people we love and to stand up when something is wrong. The monsters we imagine are only mirrors of our fears, and the heroes we admire are the people we wish to become. A child who hears these stories learns that bravery is ordinary people refusing to look away, and that lesson outlasts any single book. 🔁 Review: football, tour, volume, selection, clothing, blood, owners, guest, pool, membership, internal, approved, youth.
